selected_candidate.architecture: retain the detector's active-low static-CMOS NAND state and feed it directly into SB1, eliminating the detector output inverter and SB0

targeted_pex.ss_hot_first_failure: HSN makes a 0.753--2.945 V active-low transition, but loaded SB1 peaks at only 1.100--1.195 V and does not cross

rejected_followups.change: increase SB1 PMOS multiplicity from 8 to 12 and reduce direct BOOST inverter from MP5/MN8 to MP3/MN4
rejected_followups.conclusion: extra detector load raises the SS/hot HSN low to 0.959--1.022 V, while the reduced BOOST driver loses TT high-rail compliance

rejected_followups.change: restore SB1 and give BOOST a separate HSN predriver plus the original final driver

tooling_finding: Required internal probes now come from the versioned event contract. This removed a false 0/8 result caused by requiring HSDY and SB0 after the topology intentionally removed those nodes; replay of the same candidate then recovered its TT pass.
conclusion: Promote the active-low NAND state over the explicit-delay checkpoint because it preserves one exact TT pass with fewer devices and moves the SS/hot failure from absent HSN generation to loaded SB1 restoration. The two bounded local strength/load-partition followups do not improve extracted coverage, so another local inverter/taper sweep is not justified.
